clue.text: Patriotic Scotsman about to get politician ring

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
MP is a Member of Parliament
a bell is rung, so ring gives bell

explanation.surface: A Scottish patriot is about to give a politician a ring on the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Campbell, the Glasgow-born poet, wrote stirring patriotic songs such as 'Ye Mariners of England'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Campbell was a Scottish poet famed for his rousing national war songs.

clue.text: Futurist seen in Kent, heading for Essex

parts.note: Clark is the first name seen in the full name of Superman's alter ego, Clark Kent

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so the opening letter of Essex is taken

explanation.surface: A forward-looking thinker spotted in Kent, making for Essex next door.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent and Essex look like neighbouring English counties, but Kent is Clark Kent, Superman's everyday identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur C. Clarke was a science-fiction writer celebrated for predicting future technology such as communication satellites.

clue.text: Is it ok if men and small folk like Milo Minderbinder?

parts.note: asking 'may I' is asking whether it is ok if
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers or men
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A polite query about whether men and little people may resemble a character from Catch-22.
explanation.walkthrough: In Heller's Catch-22 the wheeler-dealer Milo Minderbinder becomes mayor of several towns around the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Milo Minderbinder holds civic office as head of many towns, making him one of a group of municipal leaders.

clue.text: British support given to little girl in Augusta?

parts.note: a rack is a frame that supports or holds things
Little Nell is the child heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: British backing goes to a young girl living in the American city of Augusta.
explanation.walkthrough: Augusta looks like the city in Georgia, but it is the first name of Lady Bracknell in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's formidable Lady Bracknell has the Christian name Augusta, so the question mark marks an example by first name.

clue.text: Puny ice elves upset valiant queenof Narnia

indicators.note: upset says the letters of the preceding words are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Feeble frosty elves trouble a brave Narnian ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'queenof' as one word; read it as 'queen of'. 'upset' rearranges the twelve letters of PUNY ICE ELVES.
explanation.definitionFit: In C. S. Lewis's Narnia books the youngest Pevensie child is crowned and known as Queen Lucy the Valiant.

clue.text: Poet who feuded with Shaw and, in part, Mabel Lockerby

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A versifier quarrelled with Shaw and also, to a degree, with someone named Mabel Lockerby.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilaire Belloc, the Anglo-French writer of verse, sparred publicly and famously with George Bernard Shaw.

clue.text: "You can hide memories, but you can't the history that produced them" (Haruki Murakami)

definitions.text: "You can hide memories, but you can't the history that produced them" (Haruki Murakami)

parts.words: "You can hide memories, but you can't the history that produced them" (Haruki Murakami)
parts.note: a quotation with one word missing after 'can't': the solver supplies the verb meaning to wipe out, the opposite of preserving

explanation.surface: A quotation from the Japanese novelist about memory and the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Murakami's Colorless Tsukuru Tazaki; the gap after 'can't' is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to wipe out or delete completely, which history resists unlike memories.

clue.text: Celebrated Idle novelabout evil old revolutionary

indicators.note: about means going around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
novel means new or fresh, signalling a new arrangement of the word idle
revolutionary means turning round, so the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: sin is evil wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A lazy book about a wicked veteran revolutionary was much praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' looks like an adjective, but it is anagram fodder. The combined letters of evil and old are read backwards; 'novelabout' is printed as one word, read 'novel about'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fêted and treated as a star is to be celebrated.

clue.text: Chap who created Po'Sandy in cliched joke on radio

indicators.note: words on radio are heard rather than seen, so the answer sounds like the word for a stale joke

parts.note: an old chestnut is a stale, overused joke

explanation.surface: The author of a story is found in a tired gag on the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles W. Chesnutt, African American author of The Conjure Woman, wrote the story 'Po' Sandy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles W. Chesnutt wrote the conjure tale 'Po' Sandy', published in 1888.

clue.text: A boy gettingtogether with tramp and little woman

parts.note: 'Boy!' and 'My!' are both exclamations of surprise
to tramp is to march, walk heavily

explanation.surface: A lad pairs up with a vagrant and a small lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boy' looks like a noun but is the exclamation 'Boy!', which 'My!' can replace. 'gettingtogether' is printed as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: She is one of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.

clue.text: A few covering up a large and seductive dancer

indicators.note: covering up says the first piece encloses the letters that follow

parts.note: a few means some

explanation.surface: A handful conceal a big, alluring performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Salome danced for Herod in the Bible and in Strauss's opera, with her Dance of the Seven Veils.
explanation.definitionFit: Salome's Dance of the Seven Veils before Herod is the archetype of an alluring performance.

clue.text: Harlem writerbreakingmandibles and jaw

indicators.note: breaking says the letters of the jawbones and jaw are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A New York author fractures someone's jawbones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges MANDIBLES and JAW; 'and' joins them and adds no letters. The words are printed run together.
explanation.definitionFit: James Baldwin, born in Harlem, wrote Go Tell It on the Mountain and many essays on race in America.

clue.text: Two grand to tour old city by southern city abroad

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the outer pair of letters goes around the rest

parts.note: K means a thousand or a grand, so two grand is two of the letter
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Two thousand pounds to travel round an ancient city next to a foreign one in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Kursk is a city in western Russia, scene of a famous tank battle in 1943.
explanation.definitionFit: Kursk is a Russian city, so foreign to the British setter.

clue.text: Nicepages written in an outlandish style in V?

indicators.note: outlandish means bizarre, so the letters are rewritten in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Pleasant pages are composed in a weird manner inside a letter V.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicepages' is printed run together; the two words NICE and PAGES are rearranged. 'in V' reads as a place, but the V is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two raised fingers in a V shape, palm outwards, make the hippie gesture for peace.

clue.text: Lead, perhaps European, in May eleventh plays

indicators.note: plays means moves about freely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A European takes part in dramas staged on the eleventh of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E into the mix: 'plays' rearranges E with MAY ELEVENTH. 'Lead' is the metal, not leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead, with its high atomic weight, is an example of a dense metal near the bottom of the periodic table.

clue.text: Churchupset about criminal leavinglikeElmer Gantry?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the overturned letters surround the next piece
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: criminal means crooked, signalling the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A congregation is troubled by a crook departing, like Sinclair Lewis's hypocrite preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Elmer Gantry is the fraudulent revivalist preacher of Sinclair Lewis's novel. Several words are printed run together: read 'Church upset' and 'leaving like Elmer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmer Gantry is a revivalist preacher, so his style is gospel-spreading, an adjective matching 'like'.

clue.text: Passion consumingultimately phlegmatic Smiley?

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so the first piece takes in the next letter

parts.note: passion is strong emotion

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of phlegmatic is taken

explanation.surface: Fervour eats away at the calm George Smiley in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Smiley looks like le Carré's spy, but it is a smiley face typed in a message.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley face typed as a symbol in a text is a classic example of a face icon.

clue.text: A mother given the sack by English carpenter

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
to hit the sack is to go to bed

explanation.surface: An English workman sacks a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given the sack' looks like dismissal; the sack is slang for bed. Adam Bede is the carpenter hero of George Eliot's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's title hero works as a village carpenter.

clue.text: Penniless artist caused row with Times-based artist

parts.note: to cause something is to make it, past tense made
a row is a line

indicators.note: based means set within, so the artist sits inside the word for times

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in two by three
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An impoverished painter started a quarrel with another painter working for The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: Madeline Bray, in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby, supports her father by painting in poverty. 'Times' is not the newspaper but the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeline Bray scrapes a living for herself and her father by selling her drawings and paintings.

clue.text: Philosophical novel aboutduck?

parts.note: on means about, concerning
duck is zero in cricket, and love is zero in tennis

explanation.surface: A thoughtful book about a waterbird.
explanation.walkthrough: On Love is Alain de Botton's philosophical novel. Duck, a cricket score of nought, becomes love, the tennis score of nought. 'aboutduck' is printed as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alain de Botton's book is a novel that analyses romance through philosophical reflection.

clue.text: Parts of lyrical work as opposedto broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the answer sounds like the preceding word

parts.note: versus means as opposed to, against

explanation.surface: Sections of a song as against what goes out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposedto' is printed as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanzas are the sections of a poem or song.

clue.text: One'sintoKafkawork dismissingendofCzech race

indicators.note: into says the first piece goes inside what follows
dismissing means getting rid of, so a letter is removed from the title

parts.note: The Trial is a novel by Franz Kafka

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of Czech

parts.note: one's means one is, giving I'M

explanation.surface: Someone gets into a Kafka book, dropping the end of a Czech running contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' drops H from THE TRIAL to leave TE TRIAL; 'into' puts IM inside. Several words are printed run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A time trial is a race against the clock, as in cycling.

clue.text: Johnson's work initially thwartednew Labour leader

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letter of thwarted is taken

parts.note: raw means new, inexperienced

indicators.note: leader means front letter, so the first letter of Labour is taken

explanation.surface: Dr Johnson's dictionary at first frustrated a new Labour Party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnson looks like Samuel Johnson of the dictionary, but it is B. S. Johnson, whose experimental novel Trawl appeared in 1966.
explanation.definitionFit: B. S. Johnson's 1966 novel bears this title.

clue.text: Bottled-up type that's in pursuit of German nurse

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following, so the piece before it comes after the others

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
i.e. means that is

explanation.surface: A repressed type chases a German nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottled-up looks like someone repressed, but a genie is a spirit literally kept in a bottle or lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The jinn of Arabian tales lives confined in a lamp or bottle until released.

clue.text: In hearing, one who grabs doomed statesman

indicators.note: in hearing means as heard, so the answer sounds like the word for a grabber

parts.note: one who grabs is a seizer

explanation.surface: Someone snatches a leader who is about to fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Julius Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar, the Roman ruler, was fated to be murdered.

clue.text: Walkers, for example, roll from side to side in ship

indicators.note: in says the rolling word goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is a steamship
to wallow is to roll about, as a ship does in rough water

explanation.surface: Hikers pitch about aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Walkers are the children in Arthur Ransome's Swallows and Amazons who sail the dinghy Swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Walker children crew the boat Swallow and so are the 'Swallows' of Ransome's novels.

clue.text: One possibly in yarn in poverty and extremely lonesome

parts.note: in need means poor, in poverty

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters of lonesome are taken

explanation.surface: Someone poor and very lonely appears in a story.

clue.text: Underwear people like the Artful Dodger picked up

parts.note: the Artful Dodger in Oliver Twist is a pickpocket, and nickers are thieves

explanation.surface: Pickpockets like Dickens's Artful Dodger lift underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' suggests pickpocketing. Nick is British slang for steal.
